properties.name: Sennacherib (Taylor) Prism
properties.displayed_at_museum: British Museum (other copies: ISAC, University of Chicago; Israel Museum)
properties.surveyor_caveat: Sennacherib claims he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem 'like a bird in a cage', not that he took the city (2 Kings 18–19; Isaiah 36–37). This is Assyrian royal propaganda: its tribute figures differ from Scripture's, and it is silent on the loss of the army in 2 Kings 19:35.
properties.support: Clay prism with the annals of Sennacherib. It describes his campaign against Judah in 701 BC and how he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem, without claiming to capture the city.

properties.name: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III
properties.caption: Jehu of the house of Omri (Assyrian name for Israel's royal line).
properties.surveyor_caveat: Caption: "Jehu of the house of Omri." The Akkadian reads Ia-ú-a mār Ḫu-um-ri-i; 'son' (mār) is Assyrian shorthand for Omri's dynasty (Bit-Ḫumri), not literal descent. Jehu actually ended Omri's line (2 Kings 9–10); a minority reads the name as Joram. Whether the bowing figure is Jehu himself or his envoy is debated.
properties.support: Limestone obelisk from Nimrud showing a king of Israel, or his envoy, bowing with tribute before Shalmaneser III. Its caption names "Jehu of the house of Omri". It is the only known image of an Israelite king or his envoy.
